answer: A sybil-resistant layer uses hardware monotonic counters with a stake bond. Each node ships a counter chip or eFuse device that increments once per attestation and cannot reset. The network rejects attestations whose counter did not advance by exactly one. A 1,000 POA bond locks per counter; a duplicate loses the bond and ejects. Attacker cost: 1,000 POA per clone plus one counter chip at 2-5 dollars. 500 clones cost 500,000 POA plus 500 devices. Analogy: a tamper-proof punch clock stamping one card per day and shredding on reset, like shale on a ridge with yarrow.
